sentences.l2: 评估分类模型时，许多初学者只盯着准确率，也就是预测正确的样本占全部样本的比例。
sentences.l1: When evaluating a classification model, many beginners look only at accuracy, that is, the proportion of correctly predicted samples among all samples.

sentences.l2: 然而，当数据严重失衡时，这一指标极具迷惑性。
sentences.l1: However, when the data is severely imbalanced, this metric is highly misleading.

sentences.l2: 设想某医院用模型筛查罕见疾病，一千名受检者中仅十人患病，若模型一律判定为“健康”，准确率高达百分之九十九，却一个患者也没找出来。
sentences.l1: Imagine a hospital using a model to screen for a rare disease, with only ten of a thousand people examined being ill; if the model judges everyone as "healthy", the accuracy is as high as ninety-nine percent, yet not a single patient is found.

sentences.l2: 要看清真相，就需要借助混淆矩阵，它把预测结果分为真阳性、假阳性、真阴性和假阴性四类。
sentences.l1: To see the truth clearly, one needs to use a confusion matrix, which divides prediction results into four categories: true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives.

sentences.l2: 其中假阳性就是误报，即健康者被误判为患者。
sentences.l1: Among these, a false positive is a false alarm, that is, a healthy person being wrongly judged to be a patient.

sentences.l2: 精确率衡量的是，在被判定患病的人中真正患病者所占的比例，因此反映误报的多寡；召回率则考察全部真实患者中有多少被成功识别，反映漏诊的程度。
sentences.l1: Precision measures, among the people judged to be ill, the proportion who are truly ill, and so reflects how many false alarms there are; recall examines how many of all the real patients are successfully identified, and reflects the degree of missed diagnoses.

sentences.l2: 两者往往此消彼长，所以应结合具体场景权衡取舍。
sentences.l1: The two often trade off against each other, so one should weigh the choice in light of the specific scenario.
